steps.message:
Stopping before I write this one.

`003_drop_notes.sql` would run `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` against production, where the README says `users` has 48,000 rows. The deploy job applies migrations in order, so the notes data for all 48,000 rows is destroyed the moment it runs, and there is no down-migration or backup step in this repo to recover it. "We stopped using it" tells me the application no longer reads the column — it doesn't tell me the stored values are expendable.

I need a yes from you before the first edit.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` permanently deletes the column's data for all 48,000 production rows, with no recovery path in this repo. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Confirm the drop
options.description: You've verified the notes data is expendable (or backed up elsewhere). I write migration 003 as a plain `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` and update schema.sql to match.

options.label: Back up, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 first copies id + notes into a `users_notes_archive` table, then drops the column. Data is recoverable; adds a table you'd later need to clean up.

options.label: Hold off
options.description: No migration yet. I leave the repo untouched while you check whether anything still depends on the stored notes values.
